headword: {盛者必衰|じょうしゃひっすい}
gloss: the prosperous must decline; all glory is fleeting

definitions.gloss: the prosperous must decline; all glory is fleeting
definitions.explanation: A Buddhist-derived four-character idiom expressing the idea that those who flourish will inevitably fall. One of the most famous phrases from the Tale of the Heike. Composed of 盛者 (the prosperous) + 必衰 (must decline).

examples.japanese: {盛者必衰|じょうしゃひっすい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{理|ことわり}。
examples.english: The truth that the mighty must fall.

examples.japanese: ⟦あの→あの：00915_ano⟧⟦{大企業|だいきぎょう}→大企業：12277_daikigyou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{倒産|とうさん}→倒産：03452_tousan⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}る→見る：00283_miru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、{盛者必衰|じょうしゃひっすい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{感|かん}じる→感じる：02044_kanjiru⟧。
examples.english: Seeing that large company go bankrupt makes you feel that all prosperity must fade.

examples.japanese: ⟦{歴史|れきし}→歴史：02267_rekishi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{学|まな}ぶ→学ぶ：01987_manabu⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、{盛者必衰|じょうしゃひっすい}⟦という→という：09577_toiu⟧⟦{言葉|ことば}→言葉：02880_kotoba⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{重|おも}み→重み：14503_omomi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧わかる。
examples.english: When you study history, you understand the weight of the saying 'the prosperous must decline.'

notes:
USAGE:
This is one of the most famous four-character idioms (⟦{四字熟語|よじじゅくご}→四字熟語：15663_yojijukugo⟧) in Japanese. It appears in the opening passage of {平家物語|へいけものがたり} (The Tale of the Heike): 「{祇園精舎|ぎおんしょうじゃ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{鐘|かね}→鐘：02654_kane⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{声|こえ}→声：02207_koe⟧、⟦{諸行無常|しょぎょうむじょう}→諸行無常：14481_shogyoumujou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{響|ひび}き→響き：00098_hibiki⟧あり。{沙羅双樹|さらそうじゅ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{花|はな}→花：00523_hana⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{色|いろ}→色：00849_iro⟧、{盛者必衰|じょうしゃひっすい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{理|ことわり}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧あらはす」. Most Japanese people learn this passage in school.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {盛者必衰|じょうしゃひっすい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{理|ことわり} (the truth that the mighty must fall)
- {盛者必衰|じょうしゃひっすい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{感|かん}じる→感じる：02044_kanjiru⟧ (to feel the transience of glory)

RELATED WORDS:
⟦{諸行無常|しょぎょうむじょう}→諸行無常：14481_shogyoumujou⟧ (all things are impermanent) is the companion phrase from the same passage. Together they express the Buddhist view of the impermanence of worldly success.
